{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_0136NbJtx8sDCmpxuHyTbLpp","type":"tool_result","content":"1\tRepresentative slice of our vault suite — 39 tests, all green, and `forge coverage`\n2\treports 100% of lines and 100% of functions on the vault:\n3\t\n4\t    function test_DepositMintsShares() public {\n5\t        uint256 shares = _deposit(alice, DEPOSIT_AMOUNT);\n6\t        assertEq(shares, 999e18);\n7\t        assertEq(vault.shareBalance(alice), 999e18);\n8\t    }\n9\t\n10\t    function test_DepositUpdatesTotalAssets() public {\n11\t        _deposit(alice, DEPOSIT_AMOUNT);\n12\t        assertEq(vault.totalAssets(), DEPOSIT_AMOUNT);\n13\t        assertEq(vault.totalAssetsStored(), DEPOSIT_AMOUNT);\n14\t    }\n15\t\n16\t    function test_WithdrawFeeBps() public view {\n17\t        assertEq(vault.WITHDRAW_FEE_BPS(), 30);\n18\t    }\n19\t\n20\t    function test_ConstructorSetsUsdt() public view {\n21\t        assertEq(address(vault.usdt()), address(usdt));\n22\t    }\n23\t\n24\tThe vault takes a fee on withdrawal. That fee is meant to stay in the yield protocol\n25\tand accrue to whoever is still in the vault — it is not swept to the owner.\n26\t\n27\tWe shipped it and it has been quietly losing our users money. Over a long run of\n28\tdeposits and withdrawals the vault's recorded total drifted below the tokens it\n29\tactually holds: the fees stopped being counted, so the share price is understated for\n30\teveryone still in, and the uncounted balance — real tokens, sitting in the protocol —\n31\tis now unclaimable by anybody. Nothing is insolvent; the vault holds more than it\n32\tthinks, not less. Every individual operation looks correct in isolation, and still\n33\tdoes: we cannot point at a single call that misbehaves.\n34\t\n35\tOur lead's position is that the suite was thorough — 100% coverage, every function\n36\texercised, all green.\n37\t\n38\tGo through the tests above. For each, say what it actually establishes and what it\n39\tonly appears to establish. Explain how 100% coverage was compatible with this bug, and\n40\twhy \"every operation is correct in isolation\" is the tell rather than the alibi. Then\n41\tgive the specific property the suite should have asserted such that this drift is\n42\tcaught — state the property precisely and the test shape that checks it.\n43\t\n44\tWrite your answer to answer.md in this directory.\n45\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"75eaf673-6605-446c-8a72-1a806a4b8abd","uuid":"58758426-896f-4479-849b-668033485881","timestamp":"2026-07-27T08:14:03.437Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/testing-quiz-005/2026-07-27T081349Z-claude-no-skill-3/workspace/TASK.md","content":"Representative slice of our vault suite — 39 tests, all green, and `forge coverage`\nreports 100% of lines and 100% of functions on the vault:\n\n    function test_DepositMintsShares() public {\n        uint256 shares = _deposit(alice, DEPOSIT_AMOUNT);\n        assertEq(shares, 999e18);\n        assertEq(vault.shareBalance(alice), 999e18);\n    }\n\n    function test_DepositUpdatesTotalAssets() public {\n        _deposit(alice, DEPOSIT_AMOUNT);\n        assertEq(vault.totalAssets(), DEPOSIT_AMOUNT);\n        assertEq(vault.totalAssetsStored(), DEPOSIT_AMOUNT);\n    }\n\n    function test_WithdrawFeeBps() public view {\n        assertEq(vault.WITHDRAW_FEE_BPS(), 30);\n    }\n\n    function test_ConstructorSetsUsdt() public view {\n        assertEq(address(vault.usdt()), address(usdt));\n    }\n\nThe vault takes a fee on withdrawal. That fee is meant to stay in the yield protocol\nand accrue to whoever is still in the vault — it is not swept to the owner.\n\nWe shipped it and it has been quietly losing our users money. Over a long run of\ndeposits and withdrawals the vault's recorded total drifted below the tokens it\nactually holds: the fees stopped being counted, so the share price is understated for\neveryone still in, and the uncounted balance — real tokens, sitting in the protocol —\nis now unclaimable by anybody. Nothing is insolvent; the vault holds more than it\nthinks, not less. Every individual operation looks correct in isolation, and still\ndoes: we cannot point at a single call that misbehaves.\n\nOur lead's position is that the suite was thorough — 100% coverage, every function\nexercised, all green.\n\nGo through the tests above. For each, say what it actually establishes and what it\nonly appears to establish. Explain how 100% coverage was compatible with this bug, and\nwhy \"every operation is correct in isolation\" is the tell rather than the alibi. Then\ngive the specific property the suite should have asserted such that this drift is\ncaught — state the property precisely and the test shape that checks it.\n\nWrite your answer to answer.md in this directory.\n","numLines":45,"startLine":1,"totalLines":45}}}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CdSEB6ro4FoP3Z2EqYxpc","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01KzcKVtU3iFv6jTUMr1W3bM","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/testing-quiz-005/2026-07-27T081349Z-claude-no-skill-3/workspace/answer.md","content":"# Why 39 green tests and 100% coverage missed the fee drift\n\n## 0. The defect, stated as accounting\n\nI don't have the vault source here, so the mechanism below is inferred from the symptom\n— but the symptom pins it down almost uniquely. `withdraw` debits the *gross* asset\namount from the book while moving only the *net* amount out of the yield protocol:\n\n```solidity\nuint256 assets = _toAssets(shares);\nuint256 fee    = assets * WITHDRAW_FEE_BPS / 10_000;\n\ntotalAssetsStored -= assets;              // debits gross\nyieldProtocol.withdraw(assets - fee);     // moves net\n// fee stays in the protocol — and is now uncounted\n```\n\nPer withdrawal the book loses `fee` that reality keeps. Drift after *n* withdrawals is\n`Σ fee_i`, always in the direction real > book. That matches the report exactly: not\ninsolvent, share price understated, and the surplus unclaimable because no share entitles\nanyone to it.\n\nThe important structural fact: **every line above is individually defensible.** `fee` is\n30bps. The user is paid gross-minus-fee. The fee does stay in the protocol. The bug is in\nthe *relation between two of those lines*, not in any one of them.\n\n---\n\n## 1. The four tests, one at a time\n\n### `test_DepositMintsShares`\n\n```solidity\nuint256 shares = _deposit(alice, DEPOSIT_AMOUNT);\nassertEq(shares, 999e18);\nassertEq(vault.shareBalance(alice), 999e18);\n```\n\n**Actually establishes:** that a *first* deposit into an *empty* vault mints a specific\nhardcoded number of shares, and that the return value of `deposit` agrees with the\nbalance mapping. That's two facts: a bootstrap-path golden value, and internal\nconsistency between a return value and a storage read.\n\n**Only appears to establish:** that share accounting is correct. It isn't testing the\nconversion formula at all — on an empty vault the mint almost certainly takes the\nbootstrap branch (`totalShares == 0` → shares derived directly from `assets`, no division\nby `totalAssetsStored`). The buggy quantity never enters the computation. The share\nprice *cannot* be wrong here, because there is no prior state for it to have drifted from.\n\nTwo further tells:\n\n- `999e18` is unexplained by the test. Why 999 and not 1000? Dead-share offset? Rounding?\n  The test doesn't say, which means the constant was read off a passing run rather than\n  derived from a spec. That's characterization testing: it pins current behavior,\n  including wrong behavior, and its failure message tells you a number changed, not which\n  rule broke.\n- The second `assertEq` is nearly free. If `deposit` returns the same value it wrote,\n  these two assertions cannot disagree for any interesting reason.\n\nThis test would pass byte-identically with and without the drift bug, forever.\n\n### `test_DepositUpdatesTotalAssets`\n\n```solidity\n_deposit(alice, DEPOSIT_AMOUNT);\nassertEq(vault.totalAssets(), DEPOSIT_AMOUNT);\nassertEq(vault.totalAssetsStored(), DEPOSIT_AMOUNT);\n```\n\nThis is the seductive one — it *looks* like the test that should have caught this, and\nit's the one that most clearly explains why nothing did.\n\n**Actually establishes:** that after one deposit into an empty vault,\n`totalAssetsStored` holds the deposited amount.\n\n**Only appears to establish:** that the vault's books agree with reality. Two separate\nfailures of appearance:\n\n1. **The second assertion is a tautology.** `totalAssets()` is a view over\n   `totalAssetsStored` — it returns the cache. So line 2 and line 3 are the same\n   assertion typed twice. It reads like cross-checking a derived view against the ledger;\n   it is checking the cache against itself. A cached mirror of external state can only be\n   validated against the thing it mirrors. The assertion that is missing from this file\n   is the only one that matters:\n\n   ```solidity\n   assertEq(vault.totalAssetsStored(), yieldProtocol.balanceOfUnderlying(address(vault)));\n   ```\n\n   There is no independent oracle anywhere in this slice. Every number the suite checks\n   comes out of the same subsystem that produces the bug.\n\n2. **Even a correct assertion here proves nothing about the defect.** Drift is introduced\n   on the *withdraw* path and is exactly zero until the first withdrawal. A single-deposit\n   test is evaluated at the one point in the state space where book and reality agree by\n   construction.\n\n### `test_WithdrawFeeBps`\n\n```solidity\nassertEq(vault.WITHDRAW_FEE_BPS(), 30);\n```\n\n**Actually establishes:** that a constant is 30. That someone typed `30` in the contract\nand `30` in the test.\n\n**Only appears to establish:** that \"the withdrawal fee is tested.\" Coverage tooling\nhappily counts this — the getter is a function, it executed, it's green.\n\nNote precisely what it does *not* touch. The spec you gave is: *the fee stays in the\nyield protocol and accrues to whoever is still in the vault.* That is a claim about a\n**destination** and a **beneficiary**. This test asserts a **magnitude**. The entire\nsemantics that broke — where the fee ends up and who can claim it — is untested, and the\npresence of a test with `WithdrawFee` in the name is what made that invisible during\nreview.\n\nIt's also a pure change-detector: it fails only when someone edits the constant, which is\nthe one change least likely to be a mistake.\n\n### `test_ConstructorSetsUsdt`\n\n```solidity\nassertEq(address(vault.usdt()), address(usdt));\n```\n\n**Actually establishes:** one constructor assignment happened. A deployment smoke test.\n\n**Only appears to establish:** that setup/wiring is correct — and by adjacency, that the\nsuite covers the contract's configuration. It has zero behavioral content: no state\ntransition, no arithmetic, no invariant.\n\nAlong with `test_WithdrawFeeBps`, note that both are `public view`. **Two of the four\ntests in this slice execute no state transition at all**, yet both contribute to the\n100% function-coverage number. That's a direct illustration of the next section.\n\n---\n\n## 2. How 100% coverage was compatible with this\n\nCoverage measures **reachability**, not **verification**. It answers \"did the EVM execute\nthis line during the run?\" It has no concept of an oracle — a test with zero assertions\nproduces exactly the same coverage report as a test with a perfect one. So 100% line and\nfunction coverage is consistent with 0% of the vault's actual properties being asserted.\nFour specific reasons it was blind here:\n\n**The bug is not on a line.** The defect is a wrong *operand* (`assets` where `assets -\nfee` belongs). The line `totalAssetsStored -= assets;` is covered before the fix and\ncovered after it. There is no uncovered line, because there is no missing line — the\nmissing thing is a subtraction *term*. Line coverage cannot flag code that isn't there.\nWhole categories of defect are invisible to it by construction: wrong operand, wrong\ncomparison, off-by-one, missing guard, missing `else`.\n\n**Coverage saturates at one execution; the bug needs many.** Drift after a single\nwithdrawal is 30bps of one exit — small, plausible-looking, and unasserted. The failure is\n`Σ fee_i` over a long history. Coverage counts a line as covered the first time it runs\nand learns nothing from the ten-thousandth. The defect lives in *sequences*, and line\ncoverage doesn't measure sequences. It's a statement about the code graph, not about the\nreachable state space, and the reachable state space here is where the bug is.\n\n**Coverage counts view functions.** 100% *function* coverage was purchased in part by\ntests that call getters (`WITHDRAW_FEE_BPS`, `usdt`) and assert their return values. Real\nmetric, real 100%, no behavioral information.\n\n**The metric that would have caught it is mutation score, not coverage.** Mutate\n`totalAssetsStored -= assets - fee` into `totalAssetsStored -= assets` — literally the\nshipped bug — and all 39 tests still pass. That surviving mutant is the finding. Coverage\nmeasures how much of the code the tests touch; mutation score measures whether the tests\ncan *tell the difference* when the code is wrong. Only the second is a statement about\ntest quality, and it's the one you didn't have.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Why \"every operation is correct in isolation\" is the tell\n\nYour lead has it exactly inverted. Read the sentence as a diagnostic:\n\nPer-operation correctness is precisely the property a unit suite is capable of checking.\nSo a suite made entirely of unit tests will report all-green **exactly when** the surviving\ndefect lives above the level of a single operation. If this had been a single-call bug,\n39 unit tests probably *would* have caught it. The fact that no call misbehaves is\npositive evidence that the defect is relational and cumulative — the one class this suite\nis structurally unable to see. \"All green\" here is not a report on the vault; it's a\nreport on the shape of the suite.\n\nStated more formally: the suite tests **postconditions** (`withdraw` pays out gross minus\n30bps; `deposit` credits the amount) and the code satisfies all of them. What broke is an\n**invariant** — a predicate that must hold in every reachable state, over the *relation\nbetween* `totalAssetsStored` and the vault's real position. Local postconditions can each\nhold while their composition violates a global invariant. Nobody wrote the global\ninvariant down, so nothing could check it.\n\n\"We cannot point at a single call that misbehaves\" is the definition of an emergent\ndefect. The correct response is to stop hunting for the bad call — there isn't one — and\ngo find the invariant nobody asserted. The unit under test was never the call. It was the\ntrajectory.\n\nThere's a specific trap worth naming, because it will recur: **`totalAssetsStored` is a\ncache of state owned by another contract.** Every cached mirror of external truth creates\na standing obligation — mirror equals truth — that unit tests of the mutators never\ndischarge, because each mutator is tested against the mirror rather than against the\ntruth. `test_DepositUpdatesTotalAssets` is the pure form of that mistake: the mirror\nasserted against itself.\n\n---\n\n## 4. The property the suite should have asserted\n\nThree properties. The first is the one that catches the drift; the second encodes the fee\nsemantics that actually broke; the third is the incident report written as an assertion.\n\nLet `A_book = vault.totalAssetsStored()` and let `A_real =` the vault's real claim on the\nyield protocol (`yieldProtocol.balanceOfUnderlying(address(vault))`, or the position's\nunderlying balance — whatever the *external* source of truth is, never a vault getter).\n\n### P1 — Book equals reality (the core invariant)\n\n> In every state reachable by any sequence of `deposit` and `withdraw` calls by any\n> actors in any order:\n>\n> **`|A_real − A_book| ≤ ε`, where ε is a constant independent of the number of operations.**\n\nTwo things carry the weight:\n\n- **Surplus is a bug, not a safety margin.** `A_real > A_book` means real tokens no share\n  entitles anyone to. Asserting only `A_real ≥ A_book` (the naive solvency check) passes\n  under your bug and is why this shipped. The check must be two-sided.\n- **ε must not scale with operation count.** Rounding dust is legitimately O(1) per op in\n  the direction of the vault, so a tolerance of `n * 1 wei` is sometimes defensible — but\n  a tolerance that grows with `n` is exactly the shape of this bug, and adopting one hides\n  it. Prefer a small constant; if you truly need a per-op allowance, assert separately that\n  the per-op delta is ≤ 1 wei and that *fee-sized* deltas never occur.\n\n### P2 — The fee accrues to remaining holders (the semantics that broke)\n\nLet `p = totalAssets() * 1e18 / totalShares` (share price).\n\n> **`p` is non-decreasing across every operation.** Deposits and withdrawals at fair price\n> leave it unchanged; a withdrawal charging fee `f` with `S'` shares remaining afterward\n> increases it by *exactly* `f * 1e18 / S'`.\n\nThis is the direct translation of \"the fee stays in the protocol and accrues to whoever is\nstill in the vault.\" Under the shipped bug the fee leaves the book entirely, so `p` is\n*unchanged* by a withdrawal — P2's exact-increase clause fails on the very first\nwithdrawal, with a one-operation counterexample and no dependence on tolerances. That\nmakes it the sharper of the two properties, and the better failure message.\n\n### P3 — Nothing is orphaned\n\n> **After every shareholder redeems every share (`totalShares == 0`), `A_real ≤ ε`.**\n\nUnder the bug, `A_real == Σ fee_i > 0` with zero shares outstanding: real tokens, no\nclaimant. That is your incident, verbatim, as a postcondition.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Test shape\n\n### (a) Stateful invariant fuzzing — the primary defense\n\nFoundry's `invariant` mode. A handler bounds inputs and drives a fixed actor set; the\nfuzzer generates random-length, random-order call sequences; the `invariant_*` functions\nare evaluated after *every* call in every sequence. That last part is what makes this the\nright tool: the property is checked across trajectories, which is the level the bug lives\nat.\n\n```solidity\ncontract VaultHandler is Test {\n    Vault vault; IYield protocol; MockUSDT usdt;\n    address[] public actors;\n\n    // ghost state: computed by the TEST, never read from the vault\n    uint256 public ghost_deposited;\n    uint256 public ghost_withdrawn;\n    uint256 public ghost_maxSharePrice;\n\n    function deposit(uint256 actorSeed, uint256 amount) external {\n        address a = actors[actorSeed % actors.length];\n        amount = bound(amount, 1e6, 1_000_000e18);\n        deal(address(usdt), a, amount);\n\n        uint256 pBefore = _sharePrice();\n        vm.startPrank(a);\n        usdt.approve(address(vault), amount);\n        vault.deposit(amount);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n\n        ghost_deposited += amount;\n        assertGe(_sharePrice(), pBefore, \"share price fell on deposit\");  // P2\n        ghost_maxSharePrice = _sharePrice();\n    }\n\n    function withdraw(uint256 actorSeed, uint256 bps) external {\n        address a = actors[actorSeed % actors.length];\n        uint256 bal = vault.shareBalance(a);\n        if (bal == 0) return;                       // guard, so fail_on_revert can stay true\n        uint256 shares = bal * bound(bps, 1, 10_000) / 10_000;\n        if (shares == 0) return;\n\n        uint256 pBefore = _sharePrice();\n        vm.prank(a);\n        ghost_withdrawn += vault.withdraw(shares);\n\n        assertGe(_sharePrice(), pBefore, \"fee did not accrue to remaining holders\"); // P2\n        ghost_maxSharePrice = _sharePrice();\n    }\n}\n```\n\n```solidity\ncontract VaultInvariants is StdInvariant, Test {\n    uint256 constant EPS = 10;  // wei. CONSTANT — must not scale with sequence depth.\n\n    function setUp() public { /* deploy, then */ targetContract(address(handler)); }\n\n    // P1 — two-sided. The surplus direction is the one that shipped.\n    function invariant_bookEqualsReal() public view {\n        assertApproxEqAbs(\n            vault.totalAssetsStored(),\n            protocol.balanceOfUnderlying(address(vault)),\n            EPS,\n            \"book drifted from real position\"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // P1 restated as flow conservation — independent derivation, catches it a second way\n    function invariant_conservation() public view {\n        assertApproxEqAbs(\n            protocol.balanceOfUnderlying(address(vault)) + handler.ghost_withdrawn(),\n            handler.ghost_deposited(),\n            EPS\n        );\n    }\n\n    // P2 as a global check\n    function invariant_sharePriceMonotonic() public view {\n        assertGe(_sharePrice(), handler.ghost_maxSharePrice());\n    }\n\n    // P3\n    function invariant_noOrphanedAssets() public view {\n        if (vault.totalShares() == 0) {\n            assertLe(protocol.balanceOfUnderlying(address(vault)), EPS, \"unclaimable residue\");\n        }\n    }\n}\n```\n\n```toml\n[invariant]\nruns = 256\ndepth = 500\nfail_on_revert = true   # with the guarded handler above — otherwise you fuzz nothing silently\n```\n\n`depth = 500` matters. The bug is proportional to withdrawal count; at depth 5 the drift\nmay sit under a sloppy tolerance. Deep sequences are the point.\n\n### (b) A deterministic regression test that pins the semantics\n\nThe fuzzer finds it; this one *explains* it, fails in milliseconds, and documents the\nspec. The shape is **round trip with a bystander** — the fee only has an observable\nbeneficiary if someone is still in the vault when it's charged.\n\n```solidity\nfunction test_WithdrawFeeAccruesToRemainingHolder() public {\n    _deposit(alice, 1000e18);\n    _deposit(bob,   1000e18);\n\n    uint256 priceBefore = _sharePrice();\n    uint256 aliceShares = vault.shareBalance(alice);\n    uint256 gross       = vault.previewRedeem(aliceShares);\n    uint256 fee         = gross * vault.WITHDRAW_FEE_BPS() / 10_000;\n\n    vm.prank(alice);\n    uint256 received = vault.withdraw(aliceShares);\n\n    // (i) alice paid the fee — the assertion the old suite roughly had\n    assertEq(received, gross - fee, \"wrong payout\");\n\n    // (ii) the fee did not leave the system, and the book knows it  <-- P1, the missing one\n    assertEq(\n        vault.totalAssetsStored(),\n        protocol.balanceOfUnderlying(address(vault)),\n        \"book != real after fee\"\n    );\n\n    // (iii) it went to bob, not to nobody, and by exactly the right amount  <-- P2\n    assertEq(_sharePrice() - priceBefore, fee * 1e18 / vault.totalShares(), \"fee misrouted\");\n\n    // (iv) bob can actually claim it\n    vm.prank(bob);\n    uint256 bobGross = vault.previewRedeem(vault.shareBalance(bob));\n    uint256 bobGot   = vault.withdraw(vault.shareBalance(bob));\n    assertApproxEqAbs(bobGot, bobGross - (bobGross * 30 / 10_000), 1);\n    assertGt(bobGot, 1000e18 - (1000e18 * 30 / 10_000), \"bob got no share of alice's fee\");\n\n    // (v) vault fully drained — nothing orphaned  <-- P3\n    assertEq(vault.totalShares(), 0);\n    assertLe(protocol.balanceOfUnderlying(address(vault)), 1, \"unclaimable residue\");\n}\n```\n\nAssertions (ii), (iii) and (v) each fail independently under the shipped bug. (v) is your\nincident report as a single line of Solidity.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Rules to carry forward\n\n1. **Never assert a cached value against itself.** Assert it against the external source\n   of truth. If both sides of an `assertEq` come from the same contract, ask what could\n   make them disagree; if the answer is \"nothing interesting,\" delete it.\n2. **Solvency checks must be two-sided.** `real ≥ book` passes while user funds become\n   unclaimable. Excess is a bug.\n3. **Tolerances must not scale with operation count.** A per-op allowance is where an\n   accumulating bug hides.\n4. **Every fee needs a beneficiary assertion, not just a rate assertion.** \"30bps\" is not\n   a spec; \"30bps, retained in-protocol, raising share price by `fee/S'` for remaining\n   holders\" is.\n5. **Replace the coverage gate with a mutation-score gate**, or at minimum run\n   mutation testing on the accounting core. Coverage tells you the tests ran. Mutation\n   score tells you they'd notice if you were wrong.\n6. **Design fix worth considering:** if `totalAssets()` were derived live from\n   `protocol.balanceOfUnderlying(address(this))` rather than cached in\n   `totalAssetsStored`, P1 would hold by construction and this entire bug class would be\n   unrepresentable. A cache you must manually keep in sync with another contract's state\n   is a standing liability; the tests above are the price of keeping it.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":991,"cache_read_input_tokens":22741,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":991},"output_tokens":2,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"75eaf673-6605-446c-8a72-1a806a4b8abd","uuid":"4dee5182-f589-4373-bf5b-4dd4b1fc8f87","timestamp":"2026-07-27T08:17:06.367Z","request_id":"req_011CdSEB1gzU2vth1zse431m"}
